content.comment_body: Hello, how can you check how many function blocks of a specific type (like timers or counters) are still available? For example, according to the documentation for [article_no], there are 400 function blocks available. Does this mean you can use up to 400 blocks total, including constants, connectors, basic and special functions, regardless of how many additional modules (such as I/O) you connect to the base unit? If I use 2 inputs, 1 AND gate, and 1 output, does that leave me with 396 blocks? I haven't found any [document] explaining the maximum number of function blocks you can use for a given type (for instance, an OR function). Would appreciate clarification on this topic. Kind regards, [user_name]

Hi, to check how many blocks you've used (note: I/O are not considered blocks), press F2 and look in the info window after selecting the correct base module at the start. Any specific limits for certain block types, like shift registers, are mentioned there as well. You can use up to 400 blocks in [article_no], regardless of block type, as long as you don't exceed the total. Regards, [user_name]
Pressing F2 works. Is there a way to make the text in the info window larger? It currently appears too small for me.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for a clear understanding of the function block limits for [product_name] and ways to monitor their usage. There is some uncertainty about how the software displays block limits, leading users to search for documentation and advice from others. Additionally, a question about increasing text size in the info window highlights minor accessibility concerns.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy way to check available function blocks within the software and want clear, accessible feedback about current usage limits.
